December 29, 1915. Mrs. Elizabeth B. Pettus may be appointed to a clerical position in the classi- fied service without reference to the civil-service rules. Mrs. Pettus is the widow of Maj. Harry L. Pettus, late of the Quartermaster Corps of the Army. The Quartermaster General states that Maj. Pettus served continuously as assistant quartermaster, United States Volunteers, with the rank of captain, from June 14, 1899, until honorably discharged from the service June 30, 1901 ; that he was commissioned quartermaster in the Regular Army with the rank of captain to take effect February 2, 1901, and was promoted to major on March 3, 1911; and that his services were of the highest order of efficiency, embracing every feature of duty falling to the Quartermaster Department, all of which were performed by him in a most satisfactory and efficient manner. In view of the facts the Quartermaster General recommends the issuance of an Executive order in this case, in which recommendation the Secretary of War concurs. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation.

June 18, 1915. Mrs. Mabel P. Walker may be appointed a clerk in the classified service of the Treasury Department without compliance with civil service rules. This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury in view of the expert services rendered by Mrs. Walker under temporary appointment in that department in operating the comptometer machine, whereby much time, labor, and expense has been saved, and in view of the fact that there is no eligible register of the Civil Service Commission for employees of this character.

December 30, 1914. Mr. Calvin Satterfield, of Pennsylvania, may be appointed to the position of Chief of the Division of Accounts, Department of Justice, without reference to the civil- service rules. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Attorney General, who states that the position of Chief of the Division of Accounts is highly confidential, and requires a peculiar order of talent; that a diligent effort has been made within the classified service to find some one possessing the required qualifications, but without success. The Attorney General believes that Mr. Satterfield, who is known to him personally, is especially qualified for the position, and that the interests of the public would be subserved by exempting the appointment. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation.

January 3, 1917. Mr. Dolley Farrior may be appointed to a position as messenger, or to any position in which his services can be utilized, under the War Department, without regard to the requirements of the civil-service rules. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of War, who states that Mr. Farrior was troop quartermaster sergeant of Troop C, Tenth Cavalry; that he was wounded in the right wrist in action at Carrizal, Mexico, June 21, 1916, as a result of which his right hand is paralyzed, the bullet having severed the nerve; that he was discharged on surgeon’s certificate of disability, October 31, 1916, with character “Excellent’’; and that he is reported to be a trustworthy man as shown by his being troop quartermaster sergeant, a position involving responsibility under the captain for all the property of the troop.

November 23, 1925. Mrs. Myrtle L. Clayton may be appointed as a printer's assistant in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without compliance with the provisions of the civil-service rules. This appointment is recommended by the Secretary of the Treasury in view of the fact that Mrs. Clayton is the widow of Percy B. Clayton, who served in the bureau as an electrician to the time of his death on October 24, 1925, leaving Mrs. Clayton with two small children and without means of support. As the Civil Service Commission can properly recommend waivers only when • the procedure under the rules will not fully meet the needs of the service, it is unable to concur. For charity. Her late husband was appointed a letter carrier on May 12, 1890.

February 28, 1916. : Mr. J. D. Yoakley may be reinstated to a position in the classified service without reference to the length of his separation from the service. Mr. Yoakley was appointed to a position in the post-office service in 1894 through the classified civil service, having passed the prescribed examination. He remained in this position for a period of about five years, during which time it is stated he rendered faithful, efficient, and loyal service. His reinstatement is requested by the Postmaster General in view of the method by which Mr. Yoakley was separated from the service. The Postmaster General states that he is convinced that Mr. Yoakley is well equipped for a position in the Post Office Department. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the request of the Postmaster General. :

December 14, 1915. Mrs. Margaretta G. H. Neale may be transferred from the position of special agent in the Bureau of the Census to a clerical position in the Department of Commerce without reference to the civil-service rules. This order is issued upon recommendation of the Secretary of Commerce, who states that there has existed in the Division of Publications since September 7, 1915, a vacancy which the division has been trying to fill by selection from the editorial-clerk register of the Civil Service Commission, and that of the 12 eligibles certified by the commission, 11 have declined to accept appointment at the stipulated salary, and that the papers of the other eligible, who made a very low rating, did not indicate that he has had the necessary experience or possesses qualifications which in the opinion of the division would make him a useful employee. The secretary further states that Mrs. Neale was temporarily employed in a clerical capacity in the Bureau of the Census during the Twelfth and Thirteenth Decennial Census periods; that since February 12, 1915, she has been serving as a special agent in connection with the census of manufactures; and that in view of the efficiency and aptitude displayed by her in the performance of the various duties assigned her, he believes that she is exceptionally capable and is better qualified than would be an untrained eligible who might eventually be obtained through civil-service channels for filling the vacancy in question.

March 10, 1916. Mrs. Katherine F. Rogers may be reinstated in the classified service of the Treasury Department without regard to the length of time she has been sepa- rated therefrom. This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury, who states that Mrs. Rogers served very efficiently in the Treasury Department for 10 years, resigning her position in 1910, and that he believes on account of her experience and her high efficiency her services will be of real value to the department. Mrs. Rogers is the daughter of the late Mr. James N. Fitzpatrick, for many years executive clerk in the Division of Appointments of the department and later assistant chief of that division, and one of the most efficient and valuable employees the department ever had. Mr. Fitzpatrick has recently died, and the burden of the support of his widow and herself falls mainly upon Mrs. Rogers. In view of the facts the Civil Service Commission concurs in the recommendation for an Executive order.

February 23, 1916. Mr. Edward Rappholt may be reinstated to the position of letter carrier in the post office at New York City without regard to the length of his separation from the service. Mr. Rappholt was appointed as substitute letter carrier at St. Louis, Mo., January 2, 1902; transferred to New York City post office August 10, 1908; to the Atlanta, Ga., post office October 16, 1912; and resigned December 8, 1912. He made application for reinstatement in December, 1913. His application for reinstatement was referred to the postmaster at New York City March 11, 1914, and disapproved. This order is issued upon the recom- mendation of the Acting Postmaster General in view of the fact that Mr. Rapp- holt’s record as a letter carrier was good, and that the failure to approve his request for reinstatement in the New York City post office at a time when it could have been made in accordance with the civil-service rules was due to a local rule rather than to a departmental rule or policy. The Civil Service Com- mission does not concur in the recommendation.

November 5, 1916. The year limit upon eligibility for reinstatement is hereby waived to permit the re- instatement of Dr. Lee F. Hawley in the Department of Agriculture. The Civil Service Commission concurs with the Acting Scretary of Agriculture in recommending this order.
